observations: Kennedy et al., BMC Public Health (2014): “These issues aren't talked about at home”: a qualitative study of adolescents’ sexual and reproductive health information preferences in Vanuatu.
Study used 66 focus groups with 341 adolescents aged 15–19 on two Vanuatu islands and 12 key-informant interviews; inductive thematic analysis.

Adolescents identified gaps in information on pregnancy prevention, condoms, puberty, sexuality, and relationships; they favored peer educators and health workers, while also wanting parental communication despite barriers.
